maria (eng-releases): Quick q — for infra-only changes (config, packaging, build flags) do we always bump the patch? or do we sometimes keep the same semver and just tag a build meta?

sam (eng-releases): patch for infra-only makes sense to me. keeps consumers simple.

leo (eng-platform): i'd +1 patch for anything that doesn't change public behavior/shape. if it's strictly deploy/ops stuff, patch. if it changes defaults that could subtly change outputs, prefer minor and call it out.

jen (eng-releases): agree + annotate in release notes when it's ops-only. also consider change window: small infra patches ok during normal window, but anything that touches default model quantization or routing should go via canary.

maria (eng-releases): ok — where do we draw the line for "subtle changes"? e.g. trailing-token trimming in tokenizer bugfix — infra vs behavior?

sam (eng-releases): tokenizer bugfix could alter outputs for some prompts -> minor. if it's just packaging (build script, dockerfile) -> patch.

leo (eng-platform): short heuristic i use: would any customer-visible test/eval possibly change? if yes -> minor. if no -> patch.

maria (eng-releases): got it. what about tagging conventions? we've got lightweight tags floating around and annotated tags in some repos. i vote annotated tags for releases and include changelog snippet.

sam (eng-releases): annotated tags `git tag -a v1.4.3 -m "patch: build fixes"` and push. also add `CHANGELOG.md` entry. lightweight tags = meh for anything we might roll back to.

ci-bot: build #4567 passed on main (commit abc123).

jen (eng-releases): +1 annotated. also: for hotfixes we should use `-hotfix` or `+hotfix` metadata? prefer `v1.4.3-hotfix.1` to make it easy to find.

leo (eng-platform): prefer hyphen suffix `-hotfix.1` so `semver` tooling still parses the core version. avoid using +build meta for semantics.

maria (eng-releases): noting down: patch for ops/packaging, minor for behavioral/default changes, annotated tags, hyphen hotfix suffix. anyone opposed to adding an explicit line in the release playbook?

sam (eng-releases): yes please. small snippet: 
```
# release.sh --patch
./scripts/release.sh --type patch --changelog "packaging: fix image build"
git tag -a v1.4.3 -m "patch: packaging"
git push origin v1.4.3
```

maria (eng-releases): perfect. last q: v0.x semantics — should we treat 0.x as "pre-1.0" and be stricter? i've seen teams bump minor for anything there.

leo (eng-platform): v0.x is tricky. general rule: if we are <1.0, a minor bump can be breaking. but for our public API surfaces we should still try to avoid surprises. Recommend document: if you change API/outputs on 0.x, clearly mark breaking in release notes and notify customers + run canary for 24h.

jen (eng-releases): agreed — and treat 0.x as needing an extra approval from eng leads for any non-patch bump.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for v1.4.3-hotfix.1 -> infra-canary (3 pods).

maria (eng-releases): thanks all — i'll add this to the playbook and open a tiny PR for the release script + changelog template. tagging style and rollback steps included. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Canary healthy after 12m. 0 errors.

maria (eng-releases): once i push the playbook change i'll ping #release-notes and @oncall for visibility.

sam (eng-releases): if canary stays green, let's roll to stable at next window.

jen (eng-releases): noted for release notes: include "scope: infra" and link to PR + CI build.

maria (eng-releases): thanks — closing thread after PR.
